ios-overlays|Alerts.summary: A Plenix alert on iOS keeps the system alert’s structure and behavior: a modal card centered over a dimmed screen, a title, an optional message and text field, and one to three actions, with Cancel answering Escape and the cancel gestures, and VoiceOver kept inside the alert. The system alert takes only a tint, so the Plenix alert is drawn as a modal view with the Plenix dialog tokens: the overlay surface, an 8-point dialog radius, DM Sans at the heading and body text roles, and Plenix buttons 44 points tall with a 12-point action gap. Apple’s default is a Liquid Glass card with capsule buttons and SF Pro text.

variants.name: Confirmation
variants.swiftui: .plenixAlert(isPresented:title:message:actions:) with a Cancel and a primary PlenixButtonStyle button (system equivalent: .alert with .tint)
variants.uikit: PlenixAlertController presented .overFullScreen (system equivalent: UIAlertController(preferredStyle: .alert) with view.tintColor)
variants.appkit: NSAlert with addButton(withTitle:) for the action and Cancel
variants.use: Confirm an action the person started that needs one more decision, with Cancel beside it.

variants.name: Destructive confirmation
variants.uikit: A PlenixAlertController action with style .destructive (system: UIAlertAction(style: .destructive))
variants.appkit: NSAlert with the delete button’s hasDestructiveAction = true
variants.use: Confirm a destructive task that cannot be undone, such as deleting a file; Cancel is never the destructive default.

variants.name: Prompt
variants.swiftui: .plenixAlert with a TextField in the content (system: .alert with a TextField in the actions)
variants.uikit: PlenixAlertController with a text field (system: addTextField(configurationHandler:))
variants.use: Ask for one short input that resolves the situation, such as a new name.

variants.name: Stacked actions
variants.swiftui: The actions in a VStack(spacing: Plenix.Platform.dialogActionGap) when there are three, or when the titles do not fit side by side
variants.uikit: PlenixAlertController with axis .vertical (the system stacks on its own)
variants.appkit: NSAlert stacks its buttons in a column when there are three
variants.use: Three actions, or two whose titles are too long for one row at the current text size.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.about: The modal card over the dimmed screen; it holds the focus until an action closes it.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.about: What happened and why, in two lines at most, in DM Sans semibold at the heading text role.

anatomy.name: Message
anatomy.about: Optional body text that helps the decision, at the secondary text role in the muted content color.

anatomy.name: Text field
anatomy.about: Optional input, shown only when the answer needs it.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.about: One to three Plenix buttons: Cancel and the preferred action, side by side or stacked.

swiftui: /// The Plenix alert on iOS: the system alert’s structure and behavior, drawn with the Plenix dialog tokens.
.frame(maxWidth: 270)   // Apple: the system alert width; on mobile the platform guideline wins
// In a view (presented with .fullScreenCover and a clear background, or the system .alert with .tint)
PlenixAlert(title: "Delete “Q3 report”?", message: "This can’t be undone.") {
// The system alert, when only the tint may change
uikit: /// The Plenix alert in UIKit: a modal card over a dimming view, with Plenix buttons (UIButton.Configuration.plenix).
card.directionalLayoutMargins = NSDirectionalEdgeInsets(top: Plenix.Space.spaceInsetXl, leading: Plenix.Space.spaceInsetXl, bottom: Plenix.Space.spaceInsetXl, trailing: Plenix.Space.spaceInsetXl)
override func accessibilityPerformEscape() -> Bool { dismiss(animated: true); return true }
// The system alert, when only the tint may change
let alert = UIAlertController(title: "Delete “Q3 report”?", message: nil, preferredStyle: .alert)
appkit: // The Plenix alert on the Mac. A Mac Catalyst app uses the iOS tokens and the UIKit code above. A native AppKit app
// needs a macOS build of PlenixTokens.swift (it uses UIColor today; the macOS build is not generated yet). NSAlert
// keeps the system look; the Plenix part is the words, the order and the destructive marking.
alert.beginSheetModal(for: window) { response in if response == .alertFirstButtonReturn { deleteReport() } }
